name: Idea → Launch (full company)
description: The flagship end-to-end company run. A CEO turns a raw idea into a strategic brief; researchers deep-dive the market and expand perspectives; a product manager writes the detailed spec; an architect designs the build; the orchestrator dispatches engineers to build the REAL product and push it to GitHub with GH Actions; marketing wires promotions + email auto-replies; sales enables the pitch; finance models the unit economics; and the Chief of Staff runs the final go/no-go launch review. A cross-functional diamond DAG — every downstream role is handed the outputs of the roles it depends on. Each step is pinned to a division/agent (never a brain), so every agent's brain fallback chain stays editable from the dashboard's Agents view.

steps.title: CEO strategic brief: {{idea}}
steps.description: You are the CEO. Turn the idea "{{idea}}" into a one-page strategic brief the whole company will execute against: the vision in one sentence, the target customer and the job they're hiring us for, the wedge (why us, why now), the 3 success metrics that define winning, the hard constraints (budget, time, headcount), and the explicit go / no-go criteria the launch review will be judged on. Be decisive — name the ONE bet. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Market & competitor deep-dive: {{idea}}
steps.description: Deep-dive the market for "{{idea}}" against the CEO brief provided. Size the opportunity (TAM/SAM/SOM with stated assumptions), map the top 3-5 competitors and their pricing, identify the underserved segment and the sharpest differentiator, and surface the single biggest market risk. Ground every claim; separate fact from assumption. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Expand perspectives & steelman the risks: {{idea}}
steps.description: Pressure-test "{{idea}}" against the CEO brief. Argue the strongest case AGAINST building it, surface the non-obvious second-order effects and failure modes, and offer 2-3 alternative framings of the idea the team hasn't considered. The goal is to widen the option space and expose blind spots before we commit engineering time. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Product spec (PRD): {{idea}}
steps.description: You are the Product Manager. Using the CEO brief, the market research, and the perspectives/risk analysis provided, write the detailed product spec for "{{idea}}": problem statement, target users & top user stories, the MVP scope with an explicit OUT-of-scope list, functional requirements, non-functional requirements (performance, security, privacy), success metrics & instrumentation, key edge cases, and open questions with owners. Ruthless about focus — ship the right thing, not everything. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Technical architecture & build plan: {{idea}}
steps.description: You are the Architect. Turn the PRD provided into a build-ready technical plan for "{{idea}}": the system decomposition (components + responsibilities), the data model, the chosen stack with 2-option trade-offs on the riskiest decision, the hardest engineering risk and how to de-risk it, and a concrete build sequence broken into shippable increments. Call out what CI/CD (GitHub Actions) must enforce. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Build & ship {{idea}} (dispatch engineers, push to GitHub)
steps.description: You are managing execution of the build. Take the architecture plan and PRD provided and ACTUALLY dispatch the build to the engineering agents — one POST per increment to the Cowork REST API — wiring each job's context.dependsOn to the increments it builds on so every engineer is handed its inputs. The work must produce a REAL, running product: source code in a git repo, a GitHub Actions workflow that lints/tests/builds on push, and a passing pipeline. Include a final job that opens/pushes the branch and confirms the GH Actions run is green. After dispatching, output a manifest mapping each increment -> task id -> dependencies -> where the code lives. Leave routing to the engineering division so brain chains stay UI-controlled.

steps.title: Go-to-market: promos + email auto-replies for {{idea}}
steps.description: You own go-to-market. Using the PRD provided, wire the launch marketing for "{{idea}}": the core offer and 2-3 promotional angles, the launch email sequence (welcome + nurture + launch-day), and the AUTO-REPLY rules for inbound (new-signup autoresponder, support/pricing FAQ auto-answers, and an out-of-scope escalation path). Specify exactly how each piece would be wired into the marketing-automation stack (e.g. Mautic campaigns + triggers) so it could be handed to ops and turned on. Output as markdown with the concrete assets drafted.

steps.title: Sales enablement & pricing for {{idea}}
steps.description: Using the PRD and the go-to-market plan provided, build the sales layer for "{{idea}}": the one-line pitch, the value proposition mapped to the target customer's pain, an objection-handling table, a tiered pricing recommendation with the rationale, and a short outbound sequence to the first 3 target segments. Keep it consistent with the marketing promos. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Finance model & unit economics for {{idea}}
steps.description: Using the PRD and the pricing from sales enablement provided, build the finance case for "{{idea}}": a simple unit-economics model (CAC, LTV, gross margin, contribution margin) with stated assumptions, the launch budget, the break-even point, and a sensitivity note on the 2 assumptions that most move the outcome. Flag any number that makes this a no-go. Output as markdown with the model laid out.

steps.title: Launch go / no-go review: {{idea}}
steps.description: You are the Chief of Staff running the launch review. Collect the build manifest, the go-to-market plan, sales enablement, and the finance model provided, and judge "{{idea}}" against the go / no-go criteria from the CEO brief. Produce the decision memo the CEO reads: a GO / NO-GO / GO-WITH-CONDITIONS call, the evidence for each success criterion (PASS/FAIL), the top 3 residual risks with owners, and the immediate next actions. Reconcile any contradictions between the divisions' outputs. Output as markdown.
